audit_findings.title: Finite 45Q noncash revenue may be capitalized perpetually while the related investment is omitted
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.653 million investment carrying value at 2025-12-31; $6.665 million of 2025 and $5.146 million of first-half 2026 cash distributions; recurring-OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor OE includes recognized noncash 45Q contract revenue that ends in April 2030, while cash distributions and the equity-method investment are outside operating cash flow and stakes_net is zero.
audit_findings.evidence: Consists mainly of freight revenue and includes sales of carbon oxide (“CO”) made in connection with the 45Q Transaction, as well as the noncash consideration received, which is recognized as the performance obligation associated with the CO Contract is satisfied over its term through April 2030.
audit_findings.explanation: A perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: a finite noncash revenue stream is included in the earnings base, while a filed investment and its cash distributions are not separately valued. The first effect overstates value and the second understates it. The filing does not isolate 2025 noncash 45Q revenue or establish the JV's current fair value, so the net materiality cannot be determined.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 OE to separately identified CO cash sales, deferred noncash revenue amortization, equity-method earnings and cash distributions; rerun OE without noncash amortization after April 2030 and add the remaining JV interest at a supported value without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal and replacement cost may escape owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.174 million of 2025 finance-lease principal; approximately $16.5 million or $1.55 per unit using the base operating-PV-to-anchor-OE multiple
audit_findings.mechanism: OE adds back finance-lease ROU amortization within depreciation but reported capital expenditures exclude noncash ROU additions, leaving finance-lease principal or equivalent replacement cost undeducted.
audit_findings.evidence: The Partnership recognizes operating lease expense on a straight-line basis over the lease term within Direct operating expenses (exclusive of depreciation and amortization) and Cost of materials and other and finance lease expense using the effective-interest method over the lease term within Depreciation and amortization and Interest expense, net.
audit_findings.explanation: The demonstrated 2025 omission is $1.174 million, about 1.0% of the $116.8 million anchor OE. Applying the base-case operating-value multiple reduces value by approximately $1.55 per unit, less than 1% of the $167.49 base value, and would leave the $130.80 price above the margin-of-safety threshold. Future replacement requirements remain unquantified but are not demonstrated as larger in the present record.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the OE reconciliation excludes the $1.174 million finance-lease principal, then rerun with that deduction; separately document expected renewal or replacement spending and reopen materiality if it materially exceeds the current charge.

audit_findings.title: The projected interest burden may not survive the 2028 refinancing
audit_findings.magnitude: $550 million principal; $5.5 million of annual interest for each 100-basis-point refinancing-rate change
audit_findings.mechanism: A post-2028 refinancing rate changes interest retained in equity-level OE; repayment from cash reduces the bridge addition, while equity issuance changes the unit denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: The 2028 Notes mature on June 15, 2028, unless earlier redeemed or repurchased by the Issuers.
audit_findings.explanation: The current fixed-rate interest burden is represented in OE, and no refinancing transaction has yet occurred. The 2028 maturity is nevertheless large relative to $137.456 million of bridge cash. The future effect could increase or decrease value depending on rates and the mix of debt repayment, refinancing and equity issuance.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the forecast with post-June-2028 refinancing-rate stresses, a cash-funded repayment case and an equity-funded case; prevent any cash used for repayment from also being added to equity value.

audit_findings.title: The terminal value assumes partnership tax status continues indefinitely
audit_findings.mechanism: Loss of partnership treatment would introduce recurring entity-level income tax into OE, including the earnings capitalized in terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Because a tax would be imposed upon us as a corporation, our cash available for distribution to our common unitholders would be substantially reduced and result in a material reduction in the anticipated cash flow and after-tax return to our common unitholders, likely causing a substantial reduction in the value of our common units.
audit_findings.explanation: No loss of partnership status or material entity-level tax is presently demonstrated; 2025 recorded a $0.023 million income-tax benefit on $98.639 million of pretax income. The filing identifies loss of qualifying status as a future risk that could substantially reduce distributable cash, making this a material downside to monitor rather than a current valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Confirm qualifying-income headroom under the projected business mix and rerun an entity-taxed downside case with supported federal and state rates, including the full terminal period.

audit_findings.title: Unrecognized environmental litigation could create a senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: claimed compensatory and punitive damages in excess of $5 million; UAN allocation and ultimate exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any uninsured settlement, judgment, remediation cost or deductible would be a senior cash claim deducted from the equity bridge or from OE if recurring.
audit_findings.evidence: In January 2026, a lawsuit was filed in the United States District Court for the District of Kansas against CVR Energy, CVR Partners and certain of their affiliates (collectively, the “Kansas Defendants”) by three residents of Coffeyville and a purported class of similarly situated persons seeking compensatory and punitive damages in excess of $ 5 million for nuisance and other equitable relief arising from alleged environmental abuse from operations at CVR Energy’s Coffeyville refinery and the Coffeyville Facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The lawsuit and remaining claims are demonstrated, but no liability has been recognized and the stated amount is only a minimum claim against multiple defendants. The June 2026 filing reports dismissal of the medical-monitoring claim but says remaining claims could have a material adverse effect. Allocation, punitive damages and insurance recovery are unresolved, so materiality cannot yet be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain subsequent pleadings, accruals, loss-range disclosures, insurance coverage and deductibles, and contractual allocation among defendants; deduct UAN's supported uninsured exposure in a rerun.

audit_findings.title: Related-party economics may not be arm’s-length or stable
audit_findings.magnitude: $42.316 million of 2025 affiliate expenses exposed to the arrangements; repricing effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes to affiliate feedstock, service, management or cost-allocation terms would alter recurring operating expenses in OE and therefore terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Further, some of these agreements were not the result of arm’s-length negotiations and the terms of these agreements are not necessarily at least as favorable to the parties to these agreements as terms which could have been obtained from unaffiliated third parties.
audit_findings.explanation: Current affiliate charges are already reflected in OE, and the filing does not demonstrate that recorded prices are presently above or below arm’s-length terms. The agreements' non-arm’s-length origin and termination provisions create a forward-looking stability risk. The exposed expense base is 36.2% of anchor OE, but the amount and direction of any repricing are unknown.
audit_findings.action: Benchmark Coffeyville MSA and Corporate MSA prices and allocations against third-party terms, review termination and change-of-control provisions, and rerun OE for supported adverse and favorable repricing cases.
